0 genes.

Under the approved DESeq2 analysis (design ~ Media + Strain, reference strain JBX1, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR threshold 0.05, DESeq2 default independent filtering), NO gene is significantly differentially expressed in any of the three comparisons to JBX1:
- ΔlasI vs JBX1: 0 genes with padj<0.05 (minimum unadjusted p = 0.112)
- ΔrhlI vs JBX1: 0 genes with padj<0.05 (minimum unadjusted p = 0.465)
- ΔlasIΔrhlI vs JBX1: 0 genes with padj<0.05 (minimum unadjusted p = 0.173)

Since the set of genes significant in at least one single mutant is empty, the set "significantly DE in ≥1 of {ΔlasI, ΔrhlI} but NOT DE in ΔlasIΔrhlI" is empty → 0 genes.

This is robust: even the minimum UNADJUSTED p-values are all > 0.05, so no gene is significant before multiple-testing correction (the answer is not an artifact of the FDR method). Sensitivity analyses all also give 0: pure BH without independent filtering; design ~ Strain (media pooled); a DESeq2-fitNR-style quasi-IRLS fit; and per-media (3 separate) analyses.

Why: the strain effects are small and inconsistent across the three media (mean log2FC vs JBX1 ≈ ±0.1 across all genes; median ≈ 0). The genes with the largest fold-changes are low-expression, high-dispersion genes that do not reach significance (e.g. top ΔlasI gene PA14_68150: log2FC −1.32 but SE 0.83 → p 0.11).
